outcome: Rewrite README.md so that Intentum is presented as an intent runtime for AI agents rather than an agent-ready backend: the opening states what it is, what distinguishes it from a database behind an MCP server, what it does not do, and that data is the first domain; section 7 lays out the next steps as two directions, checking the answer within data analysis and the same substrate for a second domain.
criteria: README.md opens with Intentum named as an intent runtime, a one-line positioning, and the four properties that distinguish it from a database behind an MCP server (closed language taught on refusal, deliverable declared before the work, fresh output trusted and recalled output checked, every operation an intent record), each tied to its decision record.
README.md section 7 states the next steps as two directions, data analysis and a second domain, and keeps every item of the previous remaining-work list and the with-and-without-backend comparison.
Every pointer into README.md from HANDOFF.md, docs/promo/README.md and the DataSpace README still resolves after the rewrite, with the pointers updated where an item moved.

The technical reference sections (architecture, transform language, raw query, exports, contracts, failure semantics, repository structure, running, MCP, examples, tests) keep their facts; no file outside README.md, HANDOFF.md and the DataSpace README changes, and the test suite passes.

dispositions.note: README.md opens with Intentum as an intent runtime, the one-line positioning, and four subsections (closed language taught on refusal, MADR 0002/0010; deliverable declared before the work, MADR 0007/0012; fresh output trusted and recalled output checked, MADR 0008; every operation an intent record, MADR 0001).

HANDOFF.md section pointers (1, 2, 7 and the named subsections) and docs/promo/README.md's #1-architecture anchor resolve unchanged; HANDOFF.md's 'section 7 item 9' and the DataSpace README's 'section 7 item 7' were updated to items 6 and 12.
